title: codehelion scan report
description: Machine-readable result of one codehelion scan. The complete current report contract.

groups.description: Every detected clone group, suppressed ones included, ordered by priority descending with the fingerprint as a tie-break.

siblings.description: Incomplete local mirrors keyed to their owning cohesive group. These are additive evidence, not primary group members.

near_misses.description: Bounded LSH proposals immediately below the primary estimated-Jaccard gate. Diagnostic telemetry only: these are neither findings nor group members.

root.description: Absolute path of the scanned directory.

database.description: Path of the local database holding the current snapshot.

run_id.description: Row id of the recorded scan run; absent when analysis completed but persistence failed.

headers.description: Language bare .h headers were read as. Absent when the run enumerated neither C nor C++.

settings.description: Resolved compiler settings grouped by build language and stable setting name.

unparsed.description: Tokens the parser could not attach to any structure. Absent in Fast mode, which lexes and does not parse.

files.description: Files holding at least one such token.

tokens.description: How many such tokens there are, excluding what error recovery salvaged.

share.description: Those tokens as a share of every analysed token.

excluded.description: Files the scan dropped, by cause; nothing is omitted silently.

too_large.description: Files over the configured size ceiling.

binary.description: Files identified as binary before parsing.

unreadable.description: Files the walker or frontend could not read.

walk_errors.description: Directory entries the source walker could not read.

timed_out.description: Files that exceeded the parse-time allowance.

symlinks.description: Symbolic links deliberately left unresolved by the source walker.

language_excluded.description: Source files excluded because their language was disabled for the scan.

symlink_files.description: Symbolic-link files deliberately left unresolved by the source walker.

symlink_directories.description: Symbolic-link directories deliberately left unresolved by the source walker.

baseline.description: What the baseline the scan was given did to its findings. Absent when no baseline was given.

file.description: The baseline file, as it was named on the command line.

mode.description: What the run was told to do with the frozen findings: hide them, or hide nothing and report every group against the baseline instead.

matched.description: Entries whose duplication this run still reports.

stale.description: Entries that hid nothing, the duplication they covered being gone. A number to act on with `baseline update`, not a fault.

appeared.description: Groups this run reports that the baseline never froze.

expanded.description: Frozen groups that now have more occurrences than the baseline covered.

stale_tokens.description: Tokens the stale entries repeated when they were frozen. Read beside `appeared_tokens`: a count of groups says nothing about size, so removing one large duplication that leaves three small ones behind reads as a regression without both numbers.

appeared_tokens.description: Tokens the groups that appeared repeat now.

expanded_tokens.description: Repeated tokens added across expanded groups.

gone.description: Every stale entry, so that what was removed can be read rather than only counted.

group.description: Hex group fingerprint the baseline froze.

duplicated_tokens.description: Tokens the entry repeated when it was frozen. Not a savings figure.

anchor.description: Where the entry's canonical occurrence sat, as the baseline recorded it. The code is gone, so this says where to remember it from rather than where to look now.

top_churn.description: What became of the highest-ranked groups of the run this one was compared with. Absent when there was no such run. A total counts how much duplication a tree holds rather than how much of it anyone has dealt with, so this states the part that was acted on separately.

since_run_id.description: Completed run used as the comparison point.

top.description: How many of each run's highest-ranked groups were compared.

closed.description: Groups of that run's top which this run no longer holds under this fingerprint or any successor that took over their history. A group whose history moved to a successor did not close.

entered.description: Groups of this run's top that the earlier run's top did not hold, and that did not inherit their history from one that it did.

still_ranked.description: Groups of that run's top which this run's top still holds. still_ranked, outranked, superseded and closed partition the earlier run's top exactly, so any one of them can be checked against the others.

outranked.description: Groups of that run's top which this run still holds below its top. Their content is still duplicated; other groups overtook them.

superseded.description: Groups of that run's top whose history a group of this run adopted. Deliberately not counted as closed: an adoption reported as a close would report one edit as both a fix and a fresh finding.

promoted.description: Groups of this run's top that inherited their history from a group of the earlier run's top, which is why they are not in entered.

type_3.description: Gapped groups; zero in modes that report no gapped clones.

restricted_semantic.description: Findings justified by registered semantic rules; zero in modes without compiler semantic analysis.

fragment_scope.description: How many of the total describe a run duplicated inside units that are not clones of each other; zero in modes that only compare whole units.

folded_runs.description: Duplicated runs left out of the listing because a reported whole-unit group already covers them, so the fold is visible rather than silent.

subsumed_runs.description: Duplicated runs left out because a longer run covers every one of their occurrences and classifies at least as strictly.

test_code.description: How many of the total live wholly in a test suite; zero in modes that do not build Structural units.

vendored.description: Groups hidden because every occurrence sits in a vendored tree, counted within `by_rule`. Reported on its own because this is the one rule that fires without anybody configuring it.

siblings.description: Total sibling entries serialized in the report, including entries suppressed from the default text listing.

near_misses.description: Total near-miss entries serialized in the report, including entries suppressed from the default text listing.

identity_collapsed.description: Stable identity records removed because an exact duplicate was emitted during final report assembly. Duplicate whole groups count once and their members are not counted again.

unmeasured_in_this_mode.description: Measurements deliberately unavailable in the selected mode. Fast reports identifier agreement, similarity breakdown, siblings and near misses here; Structural and Semantic report an empty array.

unused_suppressions.description: Configured suppression rules this run has to name: one that hid nothing, or a clone id whose prefix covers more than one group. A rule matching nothing reads as an instruction that took effect while the findings it was meant to cover are still reported, and a clone id covering several groups hides duplications nobody judged, so both are named rather than left to be found by accident.

matched.description: Groups the rule covers: 0 for a rule that hid nothing, and the number of groups for a clone id whose prefix covers more than one.

funnel.description: How many items each stage of the candidate pipeline passed on, in run order. A scan finds duplication by narrowing, so without the intermediate counts a run that found nothing looks like a run whose filters threw the evidence away. Stage names differ between the scan modes, and the structural run forks after candidate extraction into whole-unit verification and sub-unit run consolidation, so the list is a record of what happened rather than one arithmetic chain.

passed.description: Items handed to the next stage.

dropped.description: Items the stage dropped, by cause; a cause that dropped nothing is left out.

cause.description: Why the items were dropped, as a snake_case cause.

split_components.description: Sets of related units too large to compare as one piece, which grouping cut so its cost stays bounded. Every reported group is still cohesive; what the cut costs is the chance that two members on opposite sides of it would have been reported together.

common_signatures_skipped.description: Signature keys the sibling channel left out of its candidate index because more units in the tree share them than the rarity limit admits. A signature is evidence only while it is rare.

largest_skipped_signature_units.description: Units sharing the most widely shared signature the channel left out, or zero when nothing was left out. A maximum rather than a total, so it says whether the rarity limit was met narrowly or by an order of magnitude.

pair_budget_exhausted.description: True when the candidate-pair budget ran out and results may be incomplete.

search_truncated.description: True when one or more candidate-search resource ceilings truncated the search and findings may be incomplete.

unapplied_suppression_policies.description: Suppression policies Fast mode could not apply because it does not classify boilerplate, test-only code, or integer-width families.

guardrails.description: Ceilings lowered on the command line rather than by the configuration. Absent when the run worked under the configured ones.

profile.description: The named profile that was asked for.

parse_timeout_ms.description: Per-file deterministic parse-work budget, expressed in compatibility milliseconds. Each millisecond admits 256 input bytes; files above the resulting byte budget are excluded and counted as skipped. Not a wall-clock deadline: host load and worker count do not change what a scan reports.

helper_timeout_ms.description: Longest a compiler helper may answer for one source unit, in milliseconds.

posting_cap.description: Longest posting list or fragment class admitted to pairing.

pair_budget.description: Largest number of candidate pairs any pairing pass examined.

max_component.description: Largest related unit component refined as one group.

sibling_per_group_cap.description: Maximum siblings retained by one primary group.

sibling_total_cap.description: Maximum siblings retained by the whole run.

signature_sibling_candidate_budget.description: Largest number of signature-sibling candidates compared in one run.

signature_sibling_per_group_cap.description: Maximum signature siblings retained by one primary group.

signature_sibling_total_cap.description: Maximum signature siblings retained by the whole run.

signature_sibling_max_units_per_signatur.description: Largest number of units that may share one signature before that signature stops counting as sibling evidence.

compiler.description: What a compiler could supply about the tree. Absent in the modes that ask no compiler; present and thin means one was asked and could not answer.

not_asked.description: Files nobody was asked about: no installed helper reads their language, or nothing said which crate they belong to.

unavailable.description: Files a compiler was asked about and could not answer for, counted by reason.

diagnostics.description: Bounded helper diagnostics, counted by exact message.

restarts.description: How many times the helper had to be restarted during the run.

execution_refusals.description: Execution classes that prevented compiler coverage, with their exact scoped opt-in.

files.description: Files left without a compiler answer by this refusal.

cost.description: Information unavailable without this execution class.

permission_argument.description: Exact command-line argument that permits only this class.

scope.description: What each member is: a whole duplicated unit, or a run of statements duplicated inside units that need not be clones of each other.

statements.description: Statements each member covers, for fragment-scope groups; null for unit-scope groups, whose extent is the unit itself.

confidence.description: Minimum pairwise similarity across the group.

entropy_bits.description: Absolute Shannon entropy of the canonical occurrence's normalized-token distribution. The noise decision uses a length-normalized ratio; this raw value remains audit evidence.

identity.description: How this group relates to the run it was compared with. Absent when nothing connects it to that run, which is every group of a first scan. Removing part of a group's duplication either leaves the group with its own fingerprint or retires it in favour of a successor that inherits its history; without this, one edit reads as unfinished work and the other as a fix plus a fresh finding.

origin.description: Whether the compared run already knew this fingerprint, or this fingerprint took over an earlier group's history.

compared_with_run.description: The run this was decided against.

adopted_from.description: The predecessor group whose history an adopted group took over.

shared_members.description: Distinct member contents this group shares with that predecessor. The connection was decided on this quantity, so it is the evidence for it. Contents rather than members: several members of one group can carry the same content, and the rule that adopted the history counted contents.

compared_members.description: Distinct member contents this group was compared on: the population shared_members was counted out of. Absent when the recorded connection carries no measured population, in which case the shared count stands alone rather than being paired with a number that counts something else.

similarity.description: Null in modes that match content exactly and score no dimensions.

identifier_jaccard.description: Minimum raw identifier-set Jaccard agreement against the canonical occurrence. For fragment-scope groups and split pairs, it is triage proxy evidence for whether a shared refactoring target may exist, not a similarity measure. It never affects clone detection, classification, or grouping; priority uses it only as weak refactoring-difficulty evidence.

body_materiality.description: Conservative syntactic work shared by every member; maintenance evidence, not a generated-code-size prediction.

boilerplate.description: The boilerplate shape matching at least four fifths of members; null when no shape is dominant. Individual member classifications retain the exceptions.

test_code.description: Whether every member is test code. False for a group spanning a test and the code it exercises: that duplication crosses the boundary.

test_code_evidence.description: Why the group is test code: marker wins when any member has source-marker evidence; path means every member is recognised from a configured test path; null means the group is not wholly test code.

width_family.description: Whether members differ only by integer width; false when no such width family was recognised.

split_pair.description: Whether this is a verified pair reported on its own because no group could hold both members. Being a clone is not transitive, so a unit can be a copy of two units that are not copies of each other, and only one such relation fits in a group. These are the only findings whose members also appear in other findings.

ranked_down.description: Whether the effective policy placed this finding after ordinary findings.

suppressed.description: Null when the group is visible in default reports.

baseline.description: What the baseline the run was given says about this group. Absent when the run was given none.

state.description: Whether the baseline froze this group, or froze it with fewer occurrences.

added_instances.description: Occurrences beyond the baseline's covered count for an expanded group.

derived_from.description: The entry that has gone from the same places, when one has. Removing a duplication rewrites the code around it, so the groups that come out of the rearrangement are new groups with new ids; this says the new one stands where the old one stood, which is what keeps progress from reading as a regression. A claim about places, not identity.

shared_sites.description: How many of this group's occurrences sit where that entry's did.

artifact_savings.description: Artifact-correlated refactoring estimates for this clone group; estimates are not guarantees.

basis.description: Independent candidate channel that supplied this sibling. Optional for compatibility with older v1 reports.

signature.description: Exact normalized signature for signature-channel siblings.

signature_units.description: How many units in the tree share that signature. A signature is evidence only while it is rare, so the count travels with the finding and the reader weighs it; it never moves confidence_band. Null for a similarity-channel sibling, which carries no signature.

priority.description: Where the group belongs in the report, as separated measures. The composed value never appears without them, and every measure is computed from the group alone, so the same group ranks the same in every run it appears in.

clone_confidence.description: How sure the finding is duplication worth reporting.

maintenance_risk.description: What keeping the copies in step costs.

refactoring_difficulty.description: What removing the duplication would cost.

semantic_confidence.description: Reserved for the compiler backends. Absent until one measures it.

source_artifact_confidence.description: Reserved for the artifact backends. Absent until one measures it.

savings_confidence.description: Reserved. Absent: nothing measures savings yet, and a number here would read as a guarantee.

similarity.description: Per-dimension similarity evidence. Every dimension stays visible; the composite never replaces the breakdown, and an unavailable dimension is null rather than a guessed number.

weight_version.description: Composite-weight recipe the group was scored under.

api.description: Null when neither unit calls anything, so the dimension had nothing to compare.

composite.description: Weighted mean of the measured dimensions.

min_pairwise.description: Weakest pairwise similarity inside the group: its cohesion.

reason.description: Engine noise category or suppression-rule judgement, when available.

scope.description: Suppression-rule scope, present when kind is rule.

pattern.description: Suppression-rule pattern, present when kind is rule.

active.description: Whether the stored suppression rule was active, present when kind is rule.

content.description: Content fingerprint of the matched slice. Shared by every occurrence of the same content, and unlike the finding id it does not move when the group's fingerprint does — which is what lets a report exported here be compared against a run elsewhere.

file.description: Path relative to the scan root.

unit.description: Enclosing source unit, or null for a top-level fragment with no enclosing unit.

boilerplate.description: Structural classification of the enclosing whole unit. Omitted for fragments and for units that match no conservative boilerplate shape.

language.description: Language the occurrence was read as. A bare .h header is read as whichever of C and C++ the tree is written in, so this is recorded per occurrence.

ranking.description: How the run composed its ranking. Two reports written under different weights are different orderings of the same findings, which nothing else in the document says.

recipe.description: Version of the ranking rules together with the weights applied.

priority_inputs.description: What the ranking read about the group. Reported in full so the ranking can be reproduced from the published report rather than taken on trust.

smallest_member_tokens.description: Token count of the smallest occurrence, which decides how easily the group could have matched by coincidence.

similarity.description: Minimum pairwise similarity across the group.

min_clone_tokens.description: The run's minimum clone length, which the sizes are read against.

identifier_jaccard.description: Minimum raw identifier-set agreement against the canonical occurrence, when Structural mode measured it. For fragment-scope groups and split pairs, it is triage proxy evidence for a potential shared refactoring target, not a similarity measure.

api_similarity.description: Weakest call-surface agreement, when Structural mode measured one.

has_loop.description: Whether every member contains a loop, when Structural mode measured it.

has_dynamic_allocation.description: Whether every member calls a recognised allocation API.

call_count.description: Fewest recovered call sites in any member, when Structural mode measured them.

churn.description: How often the duplicated code changed. Absent: no mode reads repository history yet.

ownership_spread.description: How many people own the copies. Absent, on the same footing as churn.
